messages.content:
You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE battle (
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    date TEXT,
    bulgarian_commander TEXT,
    latin_commander TEXT,
    result TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE ship (
    lost_in_battle INT,
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    tonnage TEXT,
    ship_type TEXT,
    location TEXT,
    disposition_of_ship TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (lost_in_battle) REFERENCES battle(id)
);

CREATE TABLE death (
    caused_by_ship_id INT,
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    note TEXT,
    killed INT,
    injured INT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (caused_by_ship_id) REFERENCES ship(id)
);

To list the historical battles in your `battle` table, you can query:

```sql
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  date,
  bulgarian_commander,
  latin_commander,
  result
FROM battle
ORDER BY date, name;
```

If you mean something more specific (e.g., only battles where ships were lost, only Bulgarian victories, a date range, etc.), tell me what filter you want and I’ll tailor the query.
focus on battles with more than 10 deaths

```sql
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.name,
  b.date,
  b.result,
  COALESCE(SUM(d.killed), 0) AS total_killed
FROM battle b
JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name, b.date, b.result
HAVING COALESCE(SUM(d.killed), 0) > 10
ORDER BY total_killed DESC, b.date, b.name;
```
also need the total number of deaths to be above 10 for all sides involved

```sql
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.name,
  b.date,
  b.result,
  COALESCE(SUM(d.killed), 0) AS total_deaths_all_sides
FROM battle b
JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name, b.date, b.result
HAVING COALESCE(SUM(d.killed), 0) > 10
ORDER BY total_deaths_all_sides DESC, b.date, b.name;
```

This treats `death.killed` as “deaths” and sums them across every ship tied to the battle (i.e., all sides represented in the `ship` records for that battle). If “all sides” means something else in your data, tell me how sides are encoded.
also need names of the battles with IDs

```sql
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.name,
  COALESCE(SUM(d.killed), 0) AS total_deaths_all_sides
FROM battle b
JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name
HAVING COALESCE(SUM(d.killed), 0) > 10
ORDER BY total_deaths_all_sides DESC, b.id;
```
I need the unique IDs for the battles too.

The battle `id` is already unique (it’s the primary key). This query returns the unique battle IDs along with the battle names (and the total deaths > 10):

```sql
SELECT
  b.id AS battle_id,
  b.name AS battle_name,
  SUM(d.killed) AS total_deaths_all_sides
FROM battle b
JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name
HAVING SUM(d.killed) > 10
ORDER BY total_deaths_all_sides DESC, b.id;
```
